meta.rule: Nothing in this file is approved for generation. Candidates require wording, attribution, visibility, atomicity, overlap, and source review before promotion.

evidence_strength_scale.1 - Poor: Legacy, ambiguous, inferred, or otherwise unsupported by the supplied documentary sources.
evidence_strength_scale.2 - Fair: Explicit in one source, but attribution, status, or outcome qualification is weak or ambiguous.
evidence_strength_scale.3 - Good: Explicit in a clear authoritative source, or supported by a strong contemporaneous artifact, but not independently corroborated.
evidence_strength_scale.4 - Strong: Explicit and corroborated across multiple relevant artifacts, or a direct primary record with unusually clear authority.

meta.source_visibility_rule: Knowledge-only source files may support proposed shareable facts, but the files themselves, raw excerpts, internal links, and source contents must never be exposed to visitors.

candidates.original_text: Ben joined Johnson & Johnson in winter 2019 as the sole member of a newly defined UX/Human-Centered Design Center of Excellence within Corporate Business Technology.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: By April–May 2020, Corporate Business Technology had formally established and launched its Experience Design Management Office to support product squads.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The early operating model positioned Experience Design to help teams identify the right product opportunities, design and test initiatives, and reveal portfolio enhancement opportunities—summarized as ‘build the right things’ and ‘build those things right.’
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s organization advocated for Experience Design to be a persistent, embedded capability in product domains rather than project-based support that appears only at isolated moments.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The Experience Design service model spanned strategy, research, ideation, prototyping, implementation support, and continuous improvement through a six-stage framework: Immersion, Insights, Ideate, Iterate, Implement, Improve.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s Experience Design practice used qualitative and quantitative evidence together, including interviews, ethnography, usability testing, surveys, behavioral analytics, and product metrics.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The practice established ongoing experience-quality measurement as part of product management, defining, baselining, and repeatedly measuring experience outcomes to guide roadmaps.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: By mid-2022, the Corporate Business Technology Experience Design team had expanded into a multidisciplinary organization with domain-aligned design leaders, designers, researchers, and external delivery partners.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The organization embedded Dual-Track Agile practices so discovery, prototyping, testing, and validation could run alongside delivery.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: By early 2025, the broader J&J Experience Design chapter reported 24 full-time designers operating at or above capacity, with substantial opportunity to extend coverage across priority products.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

review.notes: This describes the broader chapter context, not a claim that all 24 people reported directly to Ben.

candidates.original_text: At Johnson & Johnson, Ben was accountable to four divisional CIOs for experience design strategy, delivery, and portfolio alignment across a design-services portfolio exceeding $6 million.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s Johnson & Johnson team grew by 200% year over year while managing more than 45 UX design engagements.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

review.notes: The résumé is explicit, but the precise period behind the year-over-year figure should be confirmed before approval.

candidates.original_text: Ben led experience strategy and design direction across workforce-facing platforms spanning human resources, finance, procurement, global services, cybersecurity, supplier, and compliance workflows.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The organization’s later operating model shifted attention from isolated product and organizational silos toward end-to-end journeys across people, products, processes, and environments.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The 2025 chapter model promoted reusable assets—personas, journey maps or blueprints, research readouts, and experience metrics—to standardize user-centered practice, reduce rework, and increase consistency and velocity.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s teams used design systems, shared component libraries, and pattern-based interfaces to reduce redundant UI work and improve consistency across enterprise products.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Ben recruited, coached, and mentored designers and design managers and helped establish a skills-development approach for the Experience Design chapter.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

candidates.original_text: In July 2020, Ben hired a Product Experience Design Lead to help expand the Experience Design practice, mature human-centered design, and lead work across the Corporate Business Technology portfolio.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The AskGS team used a mixed-method research program—knowledge assessment, 13 participatory interviews, and a survey of 1,104 respondents—to triangulate user frustrations in a colleague support portal.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: AskGS research identified seven core frustration themes and informed 43 specific improvement recommendations illustrated through a future-state vision prototype.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: The AskGS future-state vision helped the organization decide to re-platform the portal; its target capabilities informed vendor and implementation-partner selection, and Experience Design led detailed design specification work.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: For Service Performance Reporting, the Experience Design team researched 14 participants across four regions, four service areas, and three user roles to shape a future reporting experience.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Service Performance Reporting embedded Experience Design in the squad, conducted primary research before major phases, prototyped visualizations before development, paired usability studies with releases, and surveyed users quarterly.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Compared with the prior Service Performance Reporting solution, the redesigned product reported a 114% increase in speed to insight, an 85% increase in ease of use, a 122% increase in usefulness, and a 104-point increase in Net Promoter Score.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

review.notes: Retain the source’s baseline framing and avoid attributing the outcomes solely to design.

candidates.original_text: On the Vital finance platform, the Experience Design team combined workshops, ongoing research, design, and recurring measurement to guide a product used by approximately 14,500 people over a twelve-month period.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Vital’s research program reported five quarterly surveys, 98 survey responses, nine rounds of qualitative interviews, 51 hour-long interviews, and more than 110 product recommendations.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: Vital’s 2023 North America results reported ease-of-use and usefulness scores above the cited industry benchmark, with 78/100 for ease of use and 72/100 for usefulness versus a benchmark of 68.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

review.notes: Approve only with the stated geography, time period, and confidence caveat preserved.

candidates.original_text: For the enterprise purchasing experience, Ben’s organization directed research and redesign work across purchase-request, purchase-order, invoice-status, email, and self-service touchpoints.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: The purchasing-experience team estimated that redesigned email and status-page experiences could save approximately $475,000 annually through call deflection and reduced buyer effort.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

review.notes: This is a forecast, not a realized outcome; preserve that distinction.

candidates.original_text: From late 2022 through 2024, Experience Design worked continuously with MedTech Supply Chain to launch a family of control-tower products across multiple franchises.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: In 2023, the SAGE partnership supported design of seven supply-chain products intended to reduce backorder, improve service, and improve the efficiency and experience of supply-chain users.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: SAGE control-tower design was grounded in repeated user engagement, including more than 30 feedback sessions for SWIFT, about 70 sessions for Integrate across 2023–2024, and roughly a dozen sessions for the ORC control tower.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The SAGE work reused modular patterns and existing React components across multiple control towers instead of repeatedly creating bespoke interface designs.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s organization extended capacity through design partners operating under the Experience Design team’s authority and quality oversight, with regular performance and leadership reviews.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: The Supplier Risk Sensing team used cross-functional workshops and more than ten user-feedback sessions over eight weeks to produce development-ready interface designs and a future-release backlog.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

candidates.original_text: For the Comet Change Control module, the Experience Design team used four research methods, produced 69 design recommendations, and reported a response-rate increase from 3% to 22% and a 19% usability improvement versus the legacy environment.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

review.notes: Preserve the source’s methodology and baseline qualifications when reviewing the numeric claims.

candidates.original_text: For the FIRST third-party due-diligence platform serving approximately 28,000 users across 57 countries and 24 languages, the Experience Design team used collaborative workshops, iterative prototyping, and repeated usability studies to redesign a complex global workflow.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicit, direct source statement with clear authority for this record type.

candidates.original_text: FIRST usability results rose from an initial 25% usefulness and 33% usability to later study results as high as 82.5% usefulness and 90% usability before settling at 75% usefulness and 73% usability in a 173-participant baseline survey.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

review.notes: The sequence, study sizes, and differing participant groups must remain visible; do not present this as a single before/after experiment.

candidates.original_text: For PQM360, the Experience Design team joined an existing product after its fourth release, aligned product objectives and key results with the business, established a UX-Lite baseline, analyzed the information architecture, and prepared iterative feature prototyping.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

candidates.original_text: For external identity and access management, the Experience Design team worked with product and development partners to refine a partially built portal, align it with the enterprise brand, and plan research, testing, and iterative design.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported by a clear authoritative source, but not independently corroborated in this source set.

candidates.original_text: Ben designs at multiple levels of the system: he shapes individual product experiences while also designing the operating structures, practices, measures, reusable assets, and governance that enable design quality at scale.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: Ben’s practice treated product outcomes as behavioral choices and used experience strategy and measurement to connect what users value with the business outcomes a product seeks to create.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.

candidates.original_text: By 2025, the chapter was intentionally shifting design effort earlier in the product lifecycle toward experience strategy and user research, while continuing design and measurement support.
candidates.evidence_strength_rationale: Explicitly supported and corroborated across multiple source artifacts.
